lines: When the world can't keep up, it gives up detail, never the ride's smoothness.
As the world starts, it measures your display's frame period: sixteen point seven milliseconds at sixty hertz.
Every two seconds it takes the median frame. Two slow windows in a row, over one point two times the period, and it drops one level.
When frames run three times the period or more, it drops straight to Low, so you see one change of look, not three.
The frame budget is main's, and it never raises the level again during the race. The performance design and the requirement now say the same.
From a phone to a desktop, a dropped world still fills the screen, in the drawn look.
What the tests prove: slow frames drop one level, very slow frames drop to Low, and fast frames never raise it back.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
